flashcard_questions.q: What does Risalah mean in Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: Prophethood — the belief that Allah sent messengers to guide humanity.

flashcard_questions.q: Who is called the Seal of the Prophets?
Which surah states that Muhammad is the last messenger of Allah?
Why is Adam significant in Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: He was the first human being and the first prophet.

flashcard_questions.q: What title does Islam give Ibrahim?
What did Ibrahim rebuild in Makkah with Isma’il?
Which festival commemorates Ibrahim’s willingness to sacrifice his son?
What is the Sunnah in Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: The example set by the Prophet Muhammad for Muslims to follow.

flashcard_questions.q: Which prophet received the Torah, known in Islam as the Tawrat?
Which prophet received the Psalms, known in Islam as the Zabur?
Which prophet received the Gospel, known in Islam as the Injil?
Why does the Qur’an hold supreme authority in Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: Muslims believe it alone has never been changed or corrupted.

flashcard_questions.q: What is Laylat al-Qadr in Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: The Night of Power, when the first verses of the Qur’an were revealed to Muhammad.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the Imamate in Shi’a Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: The belief that twelve divinely appointed, infallible Imams should have led Muslims after Muhammad.

flashcard_questions.q: Who is the twelfth Imam in Shi’a belief?

notes: 15 cards: 5 term→definition (Risalah, Sunnah, Laylat al-Qadr, Imamate, Khalilullah), 3 prophet→holy book (Musa, Dawud, Isa), 3 person/attribution (Seal of the Prophets, Adam, twelfth Imam), 2 belief→source (Surah 33:40, Qur’an authority), 2 practice→meaning (Ka’aba, Id-ul-Adha). Title says 'Angels and Predestination' but the body teaches Risalah, Kutub, Qur’anic authority and the Imamate — cards follow the body.
